## Natural history notes

A medium-sized orange butterfly characterized by bright orange wings with black markings above and silvery-white spots on the underside of the hindwings. In Florida, it is common in sunny open habitats such as gardens, fields, roadsides, parks, pine flatwoods, coastal areas, and forest edges where passionflower vines and nectar plants are available. Adults feed on nectar from many flowers, while the caterpillars feed on passionflower leaves, using the plant’s defensive compounds to become less palatable to predators.
